justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: VR delivery evidence growing; training certification as distinct predictor of patient outcomes not studied.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Device and platform-specific training; growing availability; moderate cost; hardware investment separate.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Growing applicability in neuro, vestibular, and pain rehabilitation; limited by equipment access.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Remote patient monitoring and therapeutic activity codes applicable; some coverage for VR-based vestibular and pain management emerging.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Limited current employer demand; growing in technology-forward neuro and pain programs.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: VR engagement is high when technology is implemented smoothly.
justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Vendor-specific XR training feeds into a small but expanding set of digital therapeutic companies.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Demand exists but is fragmented across vendors and still maturing.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Limited premium given thin evidence base and immature reimbursement.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Exposure to XR development concepts without core engineering skill.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: Provides a credible entry signal for clinicians moving into XR product/clinical roles.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: Short vendor courses relative to optionality created.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Consumers don't seek 'VR therapy' by name; it's a delivery tool, not a service patients pay premium for directly.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Novelty allows modest premium in niches (peds, neuro, pain) but tech depreciates fast and no strong consumer brand.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Still uncommon in clinics, gives a marketing angle, but no protected credential and easily copied by buying hardware.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Tech-based, so other clinicians can deliver once trained; scales reasonably across staff.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Low direct consumer recognition; patients don't search for VR-certified PTs.
justifications.business.efficiency: Training is short but hardware/software costs and content curation are ongoing; moderate-to-poor ROI for small practice.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Emerging area of interest but not a recognized credential for promotion or hiring; viewed as a research/teaching interest.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Growing publication base in neuro/peds/pain rehab; good vehicle for grants and presentations.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Useful for tech-in-rehab and neuro modules but peripheral to core DPT curriculum.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Mixed; some RCTs in stroke/pain but heterogeneous interventions and small samples limit strength.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Rarely listed in faculty job postings; not a required or strongly preferred qualification.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: No standardized cert path; time investment is mostly self-directed and variable.
